newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania Hermis Bank, EBRD to sign deal.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania Hermis Bank, EBRD to sign deal.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Tuesday it was set to sign a letter of credit facility with Lithuania's Hermis Bank.
"The EBRD and Hermis will sign a letter of credit facility on Tuesday," Ivo Gueorguiev, a banker with the EBRD's Baltic team, told Reuters.
"The EBRD will guarantee up to 75 percent of Hermis Bank's letters of credit with western commercial banks. The idea is to promote trade financing and foreign trade in Lithuania."
The EBRD, which has a 20 percent stake in Hermis Bank, recently signed a similar agreement with leading Lithuanian bank Vilniaus Bank.
Hermis Bank had an 8.46 million litas profit in the first half of 1996 versus 3.62 million litas for the whole of 1995.
Its assets rose to 400.67 million litas from 331.65 million litas in the same period.

Hermis Bank, also quoted on the local bourse, has been operating in tough market conditions as the small Baltic state recovers from a banking crisis which broke late last year with the surprise closure of two of its top banks.
